snapshot.exam_hook: 🏔️ UPSC S&T Hook: Qubit: Quantum. Li-Fi: Light. Web3: Blockchain. Edge: Local processing. 5G: Low latency. Deepfakes: AI risk.

quick_notes.title: Artificial Intelligence (AI)
quick_notes.detail: Machine learning, Neural networks. Generative AI (LLMs like ChatGPT). Ethical issues : Deepfakes, algorithmic bias.
quick_notes.explanation: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is a field of computer science that creates machines or software that can perform tasks that normally require human intelligence, such as learning, reasoning, and problem-solving. Machine learning is a subset of AI where computers learn patterns from data without being explicitly programmed for every step, while neural networks are a type of machine learning modeled loosely on the human brain's structure, using layers of interconnected nodes to process information. Generative AI is a branch of AI that can create new content, like text, images, or music, and large language models (LLMs), such as ChatGPT, are a type of generative AI trained on vast amounts of text to produce human-like responses. Ethical issues with AI include deepfakes, which are realistic but fake videos or audio created by AI that can spread misinformation, and algorithmic bias, where AI systems make unfair or discriminatory decisions because the data they were trained on contains human prejudices.

quick_notes.title: Blockchain & Web3
quick_notes.detail: Decentralized ledger technology. Web 1.0 (Read), Web 2.0 (Read-Write/Social), Web 3.0 (Read-Write-Own/Blockchain).
quick_notes.explanation: Blockchain is a type of database that stores information in blocks linked together like a chain, and it is called a decentralized ledger because no single person or company controls it; instead, many users share and verify the records. The World Wide Web has evolved through three stages: Web 1.0, the earliest version, only allowed users to read content like a digital book; Web 2.0, which we use today, lets people both read and write content, such as posting on social media; and Web 3.0, also known as the decentralized web, builds on Web 2.0 by adding the ability for users to truly own their data and digital assets, often using blockchain technology. In simple terms, Web 1.0 was read-only, Web 2.0 is read-write and social, and Web 3.0 is read-write-own, where blockchain gives users control over their own information without needing a middleman like a bank or a social media company.

quick_notes.title: Quantum Computing
quick_notes.detail: Uses Qubits (Superposition and Entanglement). Exponentially faster than classical computers for specific tasks. National Quantum Mission launched.
quick_notes.explanation: A quantum computer is a new type of computer that uses qubits instead of regular bits. A regular computer bit is like a light switch that is either on (1) or off (0). A qubit, or quantum bit, can be both on and off at the same time, a property called superposition. Additionally, qubits can be linked together in a state called entanglement, where changing one instantly affects the other, no matter how far apart they are. Because of these two properties, a quantum computer can solve certain complex problems, like cracking codes or designing new medicines, exponentially faster than any classical computer we have today. In 2023, the Indian government launched the National Quantum Mission, a program to invest in and develop this technology within the country.

quick_notes.title: Communication (5G/6G)
quick_notes.detail: High speed, Low latency, Massive connectivity. 6G aims for terahertz frequencies. Li-Fi: Light-based communication (faster than Wi-Fi).
quick_notes.explanation: Communication (5G/6G) 5G stands for fifth generation of mobile network technology, and 6G stands for sixth generation. These networks provide very high speed for data transfer, low latency which means very little delay in sending and receiving information, and massive connectivity which means they can connect many devices at once. 6G is being designed to use terahertz frequencies, which are extremely high radio waves that can carry even more data than the frequencies used by 5G. Li-Fi stands for Light Fidelity, a technology that uses light from LED bulbs to send data, and it can be faster than Wi-Fi, which uses radio waves.

quick_notes.title: Internet of Things (IoT)
quick_notes.detail: Network of physical objects embedded with sensors and software (e.g., Smart homes). Edge Computing : Processing data closer to the source.
quick_notes.explanation: Internet of Things (IoT) is a network of physical objects, like home appliances or factory machines, that have sensors and software built into them so they can connect to the internet and share data. For example, a smart home uses IoT devices such as smart thermostats or lights that you can control from your phone. Edge Computing is a method where data from these IoT devices is processed close to where it is collected, instead of sending it all the way to a faraway central server. This makes the system faster and reduces the amount of data that needs to travel over the internet.
